info.title: pricepaid
info.description:
HM Land Registry Price Paid Data — every property sale in England and Wales
since 1995 — normalised and served from a local SQLite database, enriched with
ONS postcode geography, the English Indices of Deprivation 2019 and the UK
House Price Index.

Every response is wrapped in `data`, with `meta` where there is a page to
continue. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents.

Ids are strings. They use the full signed 64-bit range, JSON numbers are IEEE
doubles in every browser, and an id above 2^53 parsed as a number comes back
with its low bits rounded off.

Enrichment is optional. Against a database that has not been enriched, the
`area` object is absent, filters on it match nothing, and `real_terms` yields
no adjusted price. GET /health reports what is loaded.

get.description:
The top of the place hierarchy, and the entry point for browsing it:
each county leads to its districts, each district to its towns.

Counties are as Land Registry records them, which means unitary authorities
appear alongside historic counties — "WREKIN" and "SURREY" are both here.

get.description:
Returns 404 for an unknown county, and for a county with no districts —
which cannot happen in loaded data, since a district is what creates its
county in the first place.

get.description:
The same town name can appear under two districts. That is the source's
meaning rather than a duplicate: LONDON in Brent and LONDON in Hackney are
different places, and they get different ids.

get.description:
With q, this is a prefix search over street and town names — a prefix,
not a substring, because LIKE 'FOO%' can use the name indexes and LIKE '%FOO%'
would scan a million street names. q takes over from the other filters rather
than combining with them.

Sales are newest first and omit their property, since it is the enclosing
object.

Grouping by imd_decile needs the deprivation dataset loaded. Sales it
does not cover — everything in Wales, which has its own incompatible index —
come back under an empty key labelled "Not covered".

get.summary: Count, range, mean and quartiles for a filtered set
get.description:
Quartiles sit alongside the mean because for house prices the two
disagree usefully: a handful of eight-figure sales pull the mean well above
what anyone actually paid, and the gap is itself the interesting number.

get.description:
Every sale carries its fully resolved address, and its area when the
geography dataset is loaded.

Pagination is by cursor rather than offset, because OFFSET makes SQLite walk
and discard every skipped row: on 30M rows the ten-thousandth page would take
seconds. Follow meta.next_cursor. The cost is that pages cannot be jumped to
out of order.

get.summary: One sale by its Land Registry identifier
get.description:
The identifier is Land Registry's own GUID with its braces stripped. It is
stable across monthly publications, which is what lets a correction find the
row it corrects.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transaction unique identifier, without braces

400.description: The id is not an integer, or the query could not be understood

500.description: The request could not be completed

Area.description: Where a property is, from the ONS Postcode Directory. Omitted entirely when the geography dataset has not been loaded.

lad_code.description: Local authority district code, e.g. E09000005. What the price index is keyed on

lsoa11.description: Lower Layer Super Output Area, 2011 census. Named for its vintage because boundaries were redrawn for 2021 and the codes do not correspond; this is the one deprivation data is published against

lsoa21.description: Lower Layer Super Output Area, 2021 census

Bucket.description: One interval of a time series.

period.description: YYYY-MM or YYYY, depending on interval

Code.description: A reference-data value with its label, so nothing has to hardcode that F means flat in one column and freehold in another.

Deprivation.description: Standing in the English Indices of Deprivation 2019. Every decile runs 1 (most deprived tenth of England) to 10. Absent outside England: Wales publishes its own index on an incompatible basis, so no row is better than a wrong one.

imd_decile.description: Overall deprivation decile, 1 being the most deprived tenth of England

imd_rank.description: Overall rank, 1 being most deprived of 32,844

key.description: The grouping value. Empty where the dimension does not cover the rows, e.g. deprivation outside England

label.description: Human-readable form, where the key is a code

next_cursor.description: Pass as ?cursor= for the next page. Absent on the last one

Place.description: A named row in the county/district/town hierarchy.

id.description: Content-hash id, as a string because it exceeds 2^53

name.description: As Land Registry records it, in upper case

PostcodeRef.description: A postcode with the parts derived at load time, so area queries are an index lookup rather than substr() over 30M rows.

outcode.description: The part before the space, e.g. NW10

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. Errors are served as application/problem+json so that a client can tell one 404 from another by its type rather than by parsing prose.

detail.description: What went wrong with this particular request

type.description: A relative reference identifying the kind of problem, e.g. /problems/invalid-query

Property.description: An address: everything that distinguishes one dwelling from another. The same property links all of its sales.

paon.description: Primary addressable object name — the house number or name

saon.description: Secondary addressable object name, e.g. a flat within a building

transactions.description: Every sale at this address, newest first. Returned only by the single-property endpoint

Summary.description: Aggregates over a filtered set. The mean and the median disagree usefully for house prices; both are given.

first_sale.description: Earliest date of transfer in the set

last_sale.description: Latest date of transfer in the set

real_price_basis.description: The month they are adjusted to, when they are

TownDetail.description: A town with its ancestors resolved, so arriving by id does not cost three more requests.

Transaction.description: One sale. Property type and tenure sit here rather than on the property because the source reports them per sale and does not always agree with itself.

category.description: A is a standard price paid, B an additional one such as a repossession or buy-to-let

id.description: The Land Registry transaction identifier, braces stripped

price.description: Price paid in whole pounds, as recorded

property.description: Omitted when the transaction is already nested inside its property

real_price.description: Price restated in the money of real_price_basis. Present only with real_terms=true, and null where the index cannot cover the sale

real_price_basis.description: The month real_price is expressed in, e.g. 2026-06
